route.name: Rio Grande - Stateline to Lee Trail
route.stateAssignment: Entire trip lies within New Mexico.
route.overlap: Intentional containment within the longer Lobatos-to-Lee Ute Mountain trip; shorter Stateline launch makes the trip New Mexico-only.

qualification.access: BLM designates Stateline and Lee Trail as Ute Mountain launches/take-outs. Southwest Paddler describes a public west-bank Stateline access and a 13-mile shorter route. The Stateline map point is interpolated on the NHD Rio Grande flowline at the 37-degree state boundary (-105.7190488243, 37.0), so the marker itself is in-channel; the trail/parking location is separate. Lee Trail uses the verified in-channel coordinate from the parent Ute route.
qualification.scoring: BLM recommends at least 300 cfs. American Whitewater's reach-specific study places 600-2,000 cfs in the optimal user-preference range. The route uses a conservative 600-1,500 cfs preferred band and 2,000 cfs upper scoring guard based on the route guide's caution that flows above roughly 1,500 cfs call for advanced/expert boaters. USGS 08251500 at Lobatos is the direct same-river gauge upstream; flow bands are planning cues, not safety guarantees.
qualification.safety: Reviewed Class II skill context, fitted PFD, cold-water protection, rescue and communication gear, wind exposure, blind-drop scouting, closure, reservation, limited exits and the steep quarter-mile Lee Trail gear carry.
qualification.camping: campingClassification=none; BLM says the Ute Mountain reach has very few camping opportunities, and rim camps require climbing steep canyon walls.
qualification.gallery: Uses a BLM public-domain Ute Mountain / upper Rio Grande gorge photo with a context-only caption.
qualification.consolidation: The route intentionally shares its 13-mile downstream segment with the 24-mile Lobatos-to-Lee route. The shorter in-state launch is an independent trip option; overlap audit reports containment and no duplicate or reversed route.
qualification.geometry: Generated route-scoped canonical geometry from the named USGS NHD Rio Grande flowline: one line / 1,275 points, maximum endpoint offset 0 ft. Targeted hydrography audit passes 2/2 endpoints (0 review, suspicious, failure or unknown).

followUp: Before deployment, verify the current Stateline trail access/reservation status, launch cap, road access, wind and live gauge. Shared downstream coverage with the full Ute Mountain route is intentional and documented.
